definition: The chain rule differentiates a composition by multiplying the rate of the outer function with the rate of the inner function. Clear layer identification prevents missing factors.
Implicit differentiation treats y as a function of x even when the relation is not solved for y. Every derivative of a y-expression carries a dy/dx factor.
The derivative of an inverse reverses input and output while taking the reciprocal of the original slope at the corresponding point. A zero original slope prevents a finite inverse derivative.

Logarithmic differentiation is useful when variables appear in both bases and exponents or when products and quotients contain many factors. Taking logarithms turns multiplicative structure into additive structure.
